definition: Intrinsic motivation, in the study of artificial intelligence and robotics, is a mechanism for enabling artificial agents (including robots) to exhibit inherently rewarding behaviours such as exploration and curiosity, grouped under the same term in the study of psychology.
details: Psychologists consider intrinsic motivation in humans to be the drive to perform an activity for inherent satisfaction – just for the fun or challenge of it.

explainer.lead: Intrinsic motivation in AI and robotics is a mechanism enabling artificial agents to exhibit inherently rewarding behaviours such as exploration and curiosity. It matters because it gives agents a drive to act beyond externally specified rewards.

tiers.eli5: It is like giving a robot curiosity, so it explores just for the fun of it rather than only for a prize.
tiers.practitioner: Robotics and RL engineers use intrinsic reward signals to push agents toward exploration and curiosity-driven behavior. A pitfall is that curiosity rewards can be gamed or distract the agent from the actual task.
tiers.paperLevel: It is a mechanism enabling artificial agents, including robots, to exhibit inherently rewarding behaviours such as exploration and curiosity, grouped under the same term as in psychology, where intrinsic motivation is the drive to perform an activity for inherent satisfaction. Limits: intrinsic rewards are not tied to task success.

explainer.example: A robot receives an intrinsic reward for exploring unfamiliar parts of its environment, prompting it to investigate them.
